objects.taxonomy_description: Adult male bird exhibiting pronounced sexual dimorphism from female. Body is compact and robust measuring 30-70 cm in length depending on species. Plumage is characterized by vivid, iridescent coloration with metallic green, blue, purple, or copper tones on the neck, breast, and tail feathers. Hackle feathers (neck plumage) are elongated, pointed, and glossy, forming a distinctive ruff around the neck. Saddle feathers (lower back) are elongated and flowing. Tail feathers are long, curved, and iridescent with a characteristic arching posture. Comb is a fleshy, serrated crest on the crown, bright red and vascularized; size and shape vary by breed. Wattles are paired fleshy appendages hanging from the lower beak, also bright red. Beak is short, curved, and keratinous with a yellow to grey coloration. Legs are stout with thick, scaled skin and a prominent posterior spur (calcified projection) on the tarsus used in combat. Feet are anisodactyl (three toes forward, one backward) with sharp, curved claws. The bird exhibits an upright, alert posture with chest puffed and tail elevated.

objects.taxonomy_description: Cylindrical stick of wax (15-30 cm tall, 2-5 cm diameter) with a central wick (cotton string) extending from the top. The wax body is smooth and uniform, available in white, ivory, or colored varieties. The surface has a matte or slightly glossy finish depending on wax type (paraffin, beeswax, soy). The top has a charred wick tip if previously burned. Taper candles narrow toward the top; pillar candles maintain uniform diameter. The base is flat for standing. Scented candles may have a slightly textured surface from fragrance oils. The overall shape is a simple vertical cylinder with a thin wick protruding from the center.

objects.taxonomy_description: Asian proboscidean measuring 250-300 cm at shoulder weighing 3000-5000 kg. Body massive with thick wrinkled gray-brown skin and sparse body hair. Head broad with twin-domed skull. Ears relatively small compared to African elephant. Trunk (proboscis) elongated and muscular with single finger-like projection at tip. Tusks present primarily in males, shorter than African species. Body barrel-shaped with arched back. Legs pillar-like with five toenails on forefeet. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.
